From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha@openforge.dev>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OpenForge: request for seed cohort credits + trial extension

Hi Nikhil,

Hope you’re well — I run community programs at OpenForge and we’re organizing a two-week remote sprint (OpenForge Community Sprint, July 12–23). We have ~25 small open-source maintainer teams (language/tooling infra) who would benefit from short bursts of model compute and a slightly longer evaluation window.

We’re looking for:
- Promotional credits (per-team token allotments, ~10k tokens each) for 25 maintainers
- A 6-month trial extension for maintainers who sign up during the sprint

In return we can offer: a co-branded blog post, a short quote from OpenForge leadership for Redwood marketing, and a small booth hour during the sprint’s opening session. We’ve attached a short proposal with participant demographics and expected usage pattern (short inference, mostly embeddings + reranking).

Can we get a sense of eligibility and if this is something Redwood can support? If yes, any rough timelines for approval and internal next steps?

Appreciate any guidance — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Ayesha Khan
Head of Community — OpenForge
openforge.dev

Attachment: openforge-sprint-proposal.pdf (proposal, 2 pages)

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha@openforge.dev>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpenForge: request for seed cohort credits + trial extension

Hi Ayesha — thanks for the note and the proposal, really helpful context.

A couple quick clarifying Qs so I can scope internally:
1) Do the 25 maintainers already have accounts with Redwood (or will they sign up during the sprint)?
2) Expected per-team daily token peak (if you have an estimate)? You mentioned embeddings + reranking — will text-gen be used for any demo apps?
3) Any legal/compliance constraints we should be aware of (e.g., projects handling sensitive data)?

I’m looping in Laura from Partnerships (cc’d) to help with the co-marketing side. If we can get those answers I’ll route this to our promotions & finance leads for a quick review — timelines for approval can be as fast as 48–72 hours if it’s within our promotional budget.

If it helps, we sometimes provide a two-step package: a pilot promo credit pool (one-time token allocation) + a limited trial extension for individual sign-ups tied to an event code.

Would you be open to that approach?

— Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
